questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose to go on exchange because for my studies the foreign university could offer more interesting courses than KU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the information since Kobe University sent out all the information on mail with easy to follow steps.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: One thing that was particular good, was the allocation of a Japanese student tutor who could help you with everything while being on exhange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university offered five different dormitories which are all random which you will get from the 3 priorities you choose. All five with different facilities and prices.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Most dormitories have either own small kitchen or a shared kitchen, and some with meal plans.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: What i think is important to know is the big price difference on the dormitories and also the distance from the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My dormitory was located 45 min walking from campus and 40 min with public transportation. The dormitory is old and maybe not the cleanest, however the rent is very cheap (5.000yen at 2024).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The system was somewhat fine, but a bit more complicated than at KU.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You receive an excel ark online which you need to fill out all the course informations yourself and then submit it by the deadline. It is a bit more complicated because you have to find all the information on their website yourself and it is especially more tricky if you are taking courses from a different faculty.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office is always open for help and they gladly do so.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I successfully reregistered all the classes i wanted, even those who were in a different faculty than the one i was connected. This I even something they tell before hand might not be possible, however it as when i arrived at the host university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just remember to read the emails with the instructions carefully.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses I ended up taking was fine and at a decent level of academia. however I was a bit disappointed in the amount of course that were offered in English, this meant I didn't have many options in order to take courses i found relevant for my situation.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was high, but not too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching style wise, it is very different compared to KU and it really depends on how each professor teaches their classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Peace Building Study
Japanese Legal System Ⅰ
Japanese Economy
Global Justice
Basic Seminar on Intercultural Communication 1
Introduction to International Relations
Seminar for Plurilinguistic Approach (Tandem)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really recommend the course "Global Justice" if you like to debat the moral questions such as: "Is it always morally right to save the lives of five people at the sacrifice of one life?" "Why can’t we be allowed to sell our spare kidney to a stranger who needs it?" and "Why, and to what extent, national borders are morally significant?".

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The electricity bill was higher than expected because it was an old dormitory and therefore the rooms was badly isolated.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: no comment.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university offered many options i believe, I just did not join any. It was not something you were officially told about.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The faculty offered quite a few trips and activities which you could join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The university had a 2 days festival at the campus, which I recommend.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Mount Rokko is a great view over the whole of Kobe city. Then if you are interested in a good onsen experience I can recommend Arima Onsen town.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy I would say since the university offeres a lot of help and information if needed and the city of Kobe is very relaxed compared to other cities of Japan. It was though also my 5th time in Japan so I am already somewhat used to the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you want to socialize, it is recommended to participate in all the extracurricular activity the university and tutors offer.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: no answer.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Going out in Osaka, since it is very close. Also going on a road trip to Shikoku.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that the campus and potentially also the dormitory is old (60s/70s) and on a mountain side so a lot of stairs.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no comments.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I took, gave me a lot of new interesting knowlegde. And then of course you will always meet some new interesting people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: No comments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No comments.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
